A1.justification: Both PDFs describe OWLEYE and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E. Full-text and rendered-page comparisons support reliable assessment.

before.justification: v1 reports original graph anomaly detection experiments, including benchmark comparisons, ablations, continual-learning case studies, and robustness analyses in Section 3 and Appendices B–C.

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark experiments, ablations, continual-learning case studies, and supplementary analyses in Section 3 and Appendices B–C.

M1.justification: Section 2 retains the same feature alignment, attribute and structural pattern dictionaries, truncated attention, training losses, and inference procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same twelve graph datasets and retain the same zero-shot, 10-shot, continual-learning, elevated-anomaly-rate, and domain-shift scenarios.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged across corresponding experiments, including BWGNN, GHRN, DOMINANT, SLGAD, TAM, CARE, ARC, UNPrompt, and the supplementary comparison variants.

E3.justification: Training/test splits, preprocessing, AUROC/AUPRC metrics, zero-shot and 10-shot procedures, and experimental configurations remain unchanged in Section 3 and the appendices.

E4.justification: The component ablations, efficiency analyses, continual-learning case studies, domain-shift tests, sensitivity analyses, and attention visualizations are unchanged, including the extensive analyses in Appendices B–C.

E5.justification: Both versions specify means and standard deviations across five trials in Section 3.1. The changed uncertainty value in Table 6 is a numerical result correction, with no change to statistical reporting practices.

E6.justification: Appendix B.1, Table 6 changes TAM's zero-shot average AUROC from 22.96 ± 3.96 to 65.10 ± 1.58. Its eight dataset-level entries are unchanged and average to 65.10, supporting a summary correction rather than a performance gain. Other results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and Equations (1)–(14) are unchanged. No formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about zero-shot cross-domain detection, feature alignment, dictionary-based continual learning, truncated attention, and superior performance.

C2.justification: Interpretations of attention maps, finetuning convergence, domain shift, and parameter sensitivity are unchanged. The future directions and broader-impact discussion also remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository link in the abstract that is absent from v1. Implementation details and hardware information in Section 3.1 and Appendix A are unchanged. The PDFs establish the added access information but cannot verify repository usability.

R1.justification: The cited works, Section 4 discussion, and positioning relative to prior research are unchanged. The bibliography contains the same entries despite pagination shifts.

P1.justification: v2 adds a code-availability sentence to the abstract and an acknowledgment of NSF support before the references. These are limited textual and structural additions; the scientific narrative is unchanged.

P2.justification: The abstract reflows around the code link, and the acknowledgment shifts reference placement across pages 11–16. Figures, captions, and table structures are unchanged; the Table 6 numerical correction is assessed under E6.

improvement.justification: v2 fixes an internally inconsistent baseline summary: TAM's revised mean in Table 6 agrees with its unchanged dataset-level AUROCs. The abstract also supplies code-access information. These improve reporting accuracy and reproducibility documentation, while the method, experimental evidence, and main conclusions remain essentially unchanged.
